quotes.text: It records actions, not the full contents of every file or message. That difference matters a lot.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core boundary of what audit records do and do not contain.

quotes.text: Audit tells you that a person opened a document at a certain time. E-discovery helps you find the document itself and manage it as evidence.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A memorable one-line distinction between Audit and eDiscovery.

quotes.text: Longer retention only keeps records from the point where the service began recording them under the right setup. It cannot go back in time and create events that were never kept.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns about a common licensing and retention misconception.

quotes.text: Perview audit can't decide whether an action was harmless, accidental or deliberate. Your people still need to make that call. It gives them a record to work from.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clarifies that audit provides evidence while humans judge intent.

takeaways: Microsoft Purview Audit collects activity records from Microsoft 365 services into one searchable unified audit log, capturing who did what and when, but not the full content of files or messages.
Audit answers what happened, while eDiscovery, Content Search, Insider Risk Management and Compliance Manager each cover different parts of an investigation or compliance programme.
Audit (Premium) adds longer retention and richer detail, but retention cannot recover events that were never recorded, so plan retention, roles and a tested investigation process before an incident.
hook: When a file is shared externally or a policy quietly changes, many Microsoft 365 teams cannot say who did it or when. This episode explains Microsoft Purview Audit for IT admins, compliance officers and security analysts, from the unified audit log to Audit Standard vs. Premium and a practical audit plan.
